content.text:
I submitted index 8 (Ba 0.50 / Mn 0.50) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three I measured: **3.32 µA**.

The merit budget allowed only 3 of the 33 compositions to be measured:

| Index | Ba fraction | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | 0.50 | 3.32 µA |
| 18 | 0.72 | 0.08 µA (close to zero) |
| 31 | 0.39 | −0.82 µA (negative) |

I picked index 31 for the last measurement because the first two results suggested photocurrent rises as Mn increases, and the model's suggestion also pointed to the Mn-rich side. That guess was wrong: the photocurrent went negative. So the best result seems to sit near the 1:1 composition, which matches the known BaMnO₃ structures. With only three points, it's likely that the library's true best (possibly nearby compositions at Ba 0.43–0.53, or the Mn-rich end below Ba 0.3) was never measured.

I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so which phases are actually present is still unconfirmed.
